sections.h2: What makes selling a house in Miramar different from other Broward cities?
sections.html:
Miramar is a large city at the southwest edge of Broward County, and a house here is assessed by the Broward County Property Appraiser while the city adds its own fees to the bill. The city's about page lists a population of 137,107 and a land area of 31 square miles.

Its limits are Pembroke Road on the north, County Line Road or Honey Hill Road on the south, U.S. Highway 441 (State Road 7) on the east, and a line half a mile west of U.S. Highway 27 at the Everglades Conservation Area on the west. The city motto is "Beauty and Progress."

For a seller, the size means neighborhoods differ a lot in age, homeowners association rules and flood exposure, so the first step is to pull your own permit and lien history rather than relying on a citywide average.

sections.h2: How did Miramar grow from a tiny town into a big city?
sections.html:
Miramar was incorporated on May 26, 1955, with fewer than 200 residents and about 2.9 square miles. Its first boundaries ran from Southwest 64th Avenue on the east to University Drive on the west, between the Dade County line and Pembroke Road.

The city history page says the name means "Look at the Sea" in Spanish and was taken from an exclusive suburb of Havana. The first mayor and council were sworn in on June 20, 1955, appointed by the Governor, and the first municipal election followed in January 1959. The city has since grown to roughly 31 square miles, which is why a house built in the 1960s and one built decades later can sit within a few miles of each other and face different permit and records situations.

sections.h2: What does Miramar charge on a property tax bill?
sections.html:
The city's Management and Budget page says the Broward County Property Appraiser sets assessed value, several taxing authorities set rates, and real property taxes are collected annually beginning November 1. It states that 35 cents of each ad valorem tax dollar goes to the city and 65 cents to other Broward taxing agencies.

Miramar charges as printed on the city's property tax page

City millageProposed to stay at 7.1172 (no change)
Fire assessment, residential unit$479.21 per year

Stormwater fee$120 per equivalent residential unit
One equivalent residential unit3,619 square feet

The millage on that page is a proposal, so ask the Broward tax office or the city for the adopted rate for the year of your closing. The fire and stormwater charges are non-ad valorem assessments that appear on the same bill but do not depend on your home's value. The city also runs a fire fee hardship exemption for qualified homeowners with a set application window each year.

sections.h2: How do permits and records affect a Miramar sale?
sections.html:
Miramar takes building permit applications through an online portal that is open at all hours, with counter help on limited weekdays. The Building Division says a residential permit usually takes about 15 business days to issue, and building fees carry an 8 percent surcharge.

Records matter at closing. The city states it is not likely to hold blueprints for homes more than 10 years past their certificate of occupancy, because state records rules let it discard residential plans after that. If you did work years ago, search for the permit now so a buyer's inspector does not find an open or expired one.

  • Call the Building Division at 954-602-3200 before starting a home improvement project.
  • An electric vehicle charger at home needs a city permit and inspection, even under a utility install program.
  • Homes in an association need association approval and a city permit for an EV charger.
  • Code case status can be checked online only by people listed as contacts on the case.

The city also offers a lien search, and the page notes that payments by check for lien searches must match the exact amount. Order one before you accept an offer so liens do not appear on the closing statement.

sections.h2: How do Florida tax and recording rules apply to a Miramar closing?
sections.html:
Broward County uses the standard deed rate of 70 cents per $100 of consideration, which the Department of Revenue says is paid to the county clerk at recording. All parties to the deed are liable for it, so the contract should name who pays.

  • Homestead exemption applications go to the county property appraiser by March 1, and the city page lists the Broward office at 954-357-6830 for exemption questions.
  • The state's TRIM notice comes in August, and a value petition is due with the clerk within 25 days.
  • The early payment discount drops from 4 percent in November to 1 percent in February.
  • Unpaid taxes become delinquent on April 1, and tax certificates are sold by June 1.

A sale resets a homesteaded property's assessment to just value on the next January 1, so a buyer's first bill can differ sharply from yours. A tax certificate holder cannot demand payment from an owner until two years after April 1 of the year of issuance, but a tax deed application can follow, so clear delinquent taxes before listing.

sections.h2: What are my choices if I need to sell a Miramar house fast?
sections.html:
Most Miramar sellers choose between listing, selling directly to a buyer, and accepting a cash offer, and the right choice depends on condition, mortgage balance and deadline. A cash offer usually trims weeks off the timeline but comes at a lower price than a retail sale, so get more than one written number.

  • Listing: widest buyer pool, with repair requests after inspection.
  • Direct sale to an investor: as-is purchase and a flexible closing date.
  • Short sale or pre-foreclosure sale: needs lender approval and starts before a judgment.

If a lender has filed suit, Florida's rules call for a sale date 20 to 35 days after final judgment, a 5 percent bidder deposit, and a 10 day objection window. Selling earlier gives you control over the price.

faqs.q: Who sets the property tax rate for a Miramar house?
faqs.a: Several taxing authorities do, and the Broward County Property Appraiser sets the assessed value. The city page shows a proposed city millage of 7.1172, so confirm the adopted figure with the city or the Broward tax collector.

faqs.q: How long does a Miramar building permit take?
faqs.a: About 15 business days for residential projects, according to the Building Division's page. Commercial projects are listed at about 30 business days.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit record from the city to sell my Miramar home?
faqs.a: Not as a general rule, but a buyer's inspector may ask for permits on past work. The city says it is not likely to keep plans for homes more than 10 years past the certificate of occupancy.

faqs.q: What is the Miramar fire assessment?
faqs.a: It is a yearly non-ad valorem fee on the property tax bill that pays for fire and emergency resources. The city prints $479.21 per year for a residential unit, and a hardship exemption is available for qualified homeowners.

faqs.q: Where can I check for liens before selling in Miramar?
faqs.a: Use the city's lien search through its Financial Services pages and ask your title company for a full title search. Pay for the lien search in the exact amount the page requires.
